gloss: like cats and dogs; bitter enemies

definitions.gloss: like cats and dogs; on very bad terms; bitter rivals
definitions.explanation: An idiomatic expression describing two people or groups who are always fighting or who cannot get along at all. Literally means "the relationship of dogs and monkeys," as dogs and monkeys are traditionally believed to be natural enemies in Japanese culture.

examples.japanese: ⟦あの→あの：00915_ano⟧⟦{二人|ふたり}→二人：00622_futari⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}だ。
examples.english: Those two are like cats and dogs.

examples.japanese: ⟦{隣|となり}→隣：01003_tonari⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧⟦{部署|ぶしょ}→部署：08187_busho⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}で、⟦{会議|かいぎ}→会議：00710_kaigi⟧⟦で→で：00502_de⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦いつも→いつも：00599_itsumo⟧⟦{対立|たいりつ}する→対立する：22172_tairitsusuru⟧。
examples.english: We're on terrible terms with the neighboring department and always clash in meetings.

examples.japanese: ⟦{子供|こども}→子供：00554_kodomo⟧⟦の→の：09472_no⟧{頃|ころ}⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}だった⟦{兄弟|きょうだい}→兄弟：00964_kyoudai⟧⟦が→が：00051_ga⟧、⟦{大人|おとな}→大人：02856_otona⟧になって⟦から→から：00504_kara⟧⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧⟦{仲良|なかよ}く→仲良い：29434_nakayoi⟧⟦なった→なる：01970_naru⟧。
examples.english: The siblings who were like cats and dogs as children became close after growing up.

notes: One of the most well-known Japanese idioms. The expression comes from the folk belief that dogs (⟦{犬|いぬ}→犬：00632_inu⟧) and monkeys (⟦{猿|さる}→猿：02213_saru⟧) are natural enemies. This motif also appears in the folk tale {桃太郎|ももたろう}, where a dog and a monkey reluctantly cooperate. Note that Japanese uses "dogs and monkeys" where English uses "cats and dogs." Always used in the pattern ～⟦は→は：00079_ha⟧{犬猿|けんえん}の{仲|なか}だ. Related: ⟦{水|みず}→水：02258_mizu⟧⟦と→と：00512_to⟧⟦{油|あぶら}→油：01693_abura⟧ (oil and water — also describes incompatibility), ⟦{仲|なか}が{悪|わる}い→仲が悪い：25621_nakagawarui⟧ (on bad terms — straightforward expression).
